newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian bonds start week steady, outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian bonds start week steady, outlook stable.

text.p: 1500 GMT -- Norwegian debt was active in the short and long ends of the curve but there was little interest in the mid-sectors, dealers said. The long end attracted early buying as some players consider the spread against German Bunds to have widened too far. "The gap narrowed by a couple of basis points but then Germany went down and we followed so there was little change over the day," said one dealer. A firmer crown earlier in the session pushed down shart rates, although the petrocurrency weakened later. Dealers said the market had discounted any rise in U.S. interest rates and looked firm near-term. "We're looking strong and stable at these levels. We will not underperform Germany over the next couple of weeks and people may look to Norway as a good alternative on the back of the currency," another dealer said.
* Norway over Bunds gap one point narrower at 25 points
* Three-month eurokrone five basis points lower at 3.45 pct
